a79b088b9e8fb76d0b1694cdd24051dd3c6b41f4.summary: Dutch investigative news article (NRC, published 2 April 2021) about a data centre in Wormer, North Holland, run by two men from The Hague. The article says the men have for years been under investigation by authorities over cybercrime, malware and child pornography on their network. It also says that in early 2012 Dutch police contacted a British security expert about the Dutch company Ecatel. The excerpt is partial and gives no technical detail.

a7a66566cdd12df0b483f89b2d64103dffa4791e.summary: ThreatLabz (Zscaler) analyses APT37 infection chains that start with a Windows shortcut or a Windows help file lure. The chains drop a decoy document, the Rust backdoor Rustonotto and the PowerShell backdoor Chinotto. A later stage delivers the FadeStealer data-theft tool, which runs inside a legitimate Windows process, collects files, keystrokes, screenshots and audio, and sends archives to C2 servers. The report says one PHP C2 script controlled all three tools.

a7118cd3cbfe2398b7e0758e54698c1cf7b28073.summary: This is a reference index for the Mimikatz malware family, published by Fraunhofer FKIE. It lists third-party reports that mention Mimikatz, from 2011 to 2025, and is not itself a threat report. The page describes Mimikatz as an open-source tool that lets users view and save authentication credentials such as Kerberos tickets. The page notes that attackers commonly use it to steal credentials and escalate privileges, and that pentesters use it to find and fix network weaknesses.

a7dcb309428c3fc28a4f2ebebcd44d4c84836cdd.summary: A ZDNet article reports that the OurMine group defaced social media accounts of the NFL and 15 of its teams during Super Bowl week in January 2020. Most tweets from the hijacked accounts came from Khoros, a third-party social media management service. Khoros said its platform was not compromised, but a customer had unauthorized access to employee accounts. OurMine has been active since 2016, is believed to be several Saudi teenagers, and has previously hijacked many celebrity and tech CEO accounts, reportedly using passwords leaked in other breaches.
